consequences_for_round: Ledger verification must NOT depend on obsidian-cli-inspector's hash column: it is size:mtime, not sha256. Use sha256sum under the vault path (read-only) as the receipt method; optionally use the inspector's size+mtime as a weak cross-check.

The inspector is safe to run read-only against the vault (fixture-verified no vault writes), but its queries are only trustworthy for: FTS search (search notes), tag listing, metadata describe, and raw SQLite inspection of the DB copy. backlinks/links/orphans/broken-links outputs must not be cited as evidence.

A vault-verification helper that shells out MUST always pass an explicit -c config with database_path+log_path under tests/ or /tmp: controlled test shows with -c + absolute log_path the tool logs to that path only (/tmp/s02-logs 57->59 files; operator config dir unchanged 64->64), while WITHOUT -c it logs to the default ~/.config/obsidian-cli-inspector/logs (62->64 files) — i.e. any seat invoking the tool with the default config writes into operator config-dir state on every call. Also never call `init init -f` or `index index` against the operator's shared DB (~/.config/.../vault.db) unless the operator opts in — indexing writes operator state, though never the vault.
Fresh-index baseline for future rounds: 7680 markdown files reachable via symlinks; 224 wikilinks; 0 resolvable. If a later round needs graph truth, it cannot come from this tool version.

Official CLI remains non-invocable; any future 'moved-to-obsidian' confirmation stays on direct vault sha256 comparison. The live socket is promising but the client shim is absent — do not build the round on it.
